brief: BofA's Michael Hartnett argues the 2026 midterms are not a regime-change election like Thatcher/Reagan 1980 or Trump/Brexit 2016. Whoever wins, the 2020s trend of political populism and fiscal excess continues (US nominal GDP up 63% in six years, from $20tn to $32tn), so his structural Anything But Bonds trade holds regardless of outcome. Most outcomes are read as risk-on: a GOP sweep is full risk-on, and the conventional GOP Senate/Democratic House gridlock is modestly risk-on, with the fiscal regime intact. The real tail is a Democratic sweep, whose odds BofA's Polymarket snapshot puts at 50%, given Trump's unusually weak 35-40% approval rating, with Ohio, Texas, Iowa and Michigan the key Senate battlegrounds. A Democratic sweep would be risk-off: higher taxes and regulation, stocks down more than 10%, lower US yields, a weaker dollar, and international equities outperforming, hedged via short financials and short USD. Yet SPX options price just a 0.82% post-election move, so BofA prefers cheap convexity, a VIX calendar call-spread collar, over paying up for index protection, with election vol cheaper beneath the index in small caps and regional banks.
